content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To try black coffee, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Read a blog post about flavor profiles (10 minutes)
Step 2. Research local specialty coffee roasters (30 minutes)
Step 3. Check the expiration date on the coffee bag (1 minute)
Step 4. Drive to the specialty coffee shop (20 minutes)
Step 5. Set the clean mug on the coaster (10 seconds)
Step 6. Inspect the coffee beans for defects (5 minutes)
Step 7. Calibrate the digital scale (2 minutes)
Step 8. Pour the brewed coffee into a carafe (30 seconds)
Step 9. Decide on a specific roast level (5 minutes)
Step 10. Write down tasting notes in a journal (5 minutes)
Step 11. Purchase a bag of whole bean coffee (10 minutes)
Step 12. Locate the burr grinder (2 minutes)
Step 13. Preheat the coffee mug with hot water (1 minute)
Step 14. Watch a tutorial on the pour-over method (15 minutes)
Step 15. Rinse the paper filter to remove paper taste (30 seconds)
Step 16. Dispose of used coffee grounds (20 seconds)
Step 17. Clean the brewing equipment (10 minutes)
Step 18. Boil fresh filtered water (8 minutes)
Step 19. Place the filter into the dripper (15 seconds)
Step 20. Wake up and clear the kitchen counter (10 minutes)
Step 21. Measure out exactly 20 grams of beans (1 minute)
Step 22. Take the first sip of the hot coffee (5 seconds)
Step 23. Zero out the scale with the dripper on top (10 seconds)
Step 24. Pour the coffee from the carafe into the mug (15 seconds)
Step 25. Open the sealed coffee bag (10 seconds)
Step 26. Select the appropriate grind size setting (1 minute)
Step 27. Wait for the water to reach 205 degrees Fahrenheit (2 minutes)
Step 28. Smell the dry aroma of the beans (30 seconds)
Step 29. Check the water level in the kettle (30 seconds)
Step 30. Clear any distractions from the room (5 minutes)
Step 31. Set a timer for the brewing process (10 seconds)
Step 32. Put on a comfortable robe (2 minutes)
Step 33. Select a clean ceramic mug (1 minute)
Step 34. Find the gooseneck kettle (2 minutes)
Step 35. Review the recipe ratios (5 minutes)
Step 36. Share a photo of the beans online (3 minutes)
Step 37. Clear the sink of any dirty dishes (15 minutes)
Step 38. Plug in the electric grinder (10 seconds)
Step 39. Open the kitchen blinds (30 seconds)
Step 40. Put the dripper on top of the carafe (10 seconds)
Step 41. Sit down at the kitchen table (30 seconds)
Step 42. Organize the coffee station (10 minutes)
Step 43. Clean the grinder hopper (5 minutes)
Step 44. Let the coffee cool for a few minutes (4 minutes)
Step 45. Add the beans to the grinder (15 seconds)
Step 46. Check the kitchen thermometer (1 minute)
Step 47. Take the beans out of the pantry (30 seconds)
Step 48. Weigh the empty carafe (30 seconds)
Step 49. Inhale the steam from the cup (10 seconds)
Step 50. Wash your hands thoroughly (40 seconds)
Step 51. Choose a brewing method like V60 (5 minutes)
Step 52. Fetch the box of paper filters (1 minute)
Step 53. Check if there is enough filtered water (1 minute)
Step 54. Locate the digital scale (2 minutes)
Step 55. Dust off the coffee equipment shelf (5 minutes)
Step 56. Wipe down the counter after grinding (1 minute)
Step 57. Set out a spoon for stirring (30 seconds)
Step 58. Reflect on the bitterness and acidity (2 minutes)
Step 59. Fill the kettle with filtered water (1 minute)
Step 60. Grind the coffee beans (45 seconds)
Step 61. Remove the spoon from the table (10 seconds)
Step 62. Grind the coffee beans into the catch bin (30 seconds)
Step 63. Record the total brew time (30 seconds)
Step 64. Adjust the chair at the table (15 seconds)
Step 65. Bloom the coffee grounds with a little water (30 seconds)
Step 66. Discard the rinsing water from the mug (10 seconds)
Step 67. Clear a space on the counter for the scale (2 minutes)
Step 68. Place the carafe under the grinder (20 seconds)
Step 69. Fold the edge of the paper filter (20 seconds)
Step 70. Start the stopwatch (5 seconds)
Step 71. Find the bag of coffee beans (2 minutes)
Step 72. Pour the ground coffee into the filter (20 seconds)
Step 73. Pour the remaining hot water over the grounds (3 minutes)
Step 74. Observe the color of the brew (1 minute)
Step 75. Clear the workspace of clutter (10 minutes)
Step 76. Swirl the coffee in the carafe (10 seconds)
Step 77. Check the power outlet (30 seconds)
Step 78. Finish the main pour (2 minutes)
Step 79. Remove the dripper from the carafe (10 seconds)
Step 80. Wait for the final drawdown of water (1 minute)
